answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the ocean hash is checked against the river checkpoint at intake, the ledge audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 317 aliases cost 232 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
